name: Splitwise: Efficient generative LLM inference using phase splitting
problem: A single LLM serving request has two phases with opposite bottlenecks — prompt computation is compute-bound and memory-bound prompt processing is bandwidth-bound — so running both on the same device wastes one of the two resources.
mechanism: Characterise the two phases and split them across different devices: prompt computation is run on a compute-dense accelerator and the memory-bandwidth-bound decode loop on a bandwidth-dense one, inside one in-flight request. Compute- and memory-optimised phases then proceed concurrently instead of alternating.
speedup_reported: Per the arXiv abstract: 1.4x higher throughput at 20% lower cost than current designs, OR alternatively 2.35x more throughput at the same cost and power budgets. Two distinct cluster configurations (same machine type vs different machine types per phase), optimised for throughput, cost, and power as three separate objectives. Baseline is described in the paper as 'current designs'; the 1.4x/2.35x pair are two different cluster configurations, not two measurements of one.

MERGED FIELD BY FIELD - nothing was silently dropped:
  mechanism: the retired record's text was materially fuller (556 chars vs 311) and is RETAINED here rather than discarded. Its text: Split the two phases of an inference request onto SEPARATE MACHINES so each runs on hardware suited to it, and provision resources independently per phase. The hard part is that splitting requires transferring the request STATE (the KV cache) from the prompt-computation machine to the token-generation machine, so state transfer is implemented and optimised over the FAST BACK-PLANE interconnect available in GPU clusters. Clusters are then designed with the same or different machine types for the two phases and optimised for throughput, cost, or power.
  speedup_reported: the two records carried DIFFERENT text for the same paper. This record's text is retained and the retired record's variant is quoted so the difference is visible: "1.4x higher throughput at 20% LOWER COST than current designs, OR alternatively 2.35x more throughput at the SAME cost and power budgets. Both figures are against 'current designs' (the paper's characterisation of pre-splitting serving systems), and the two are alternative operating points rather than cumulative - a reader must not multiply them."
